title: Arsenal’s Jack Wilshere joins Bournemouth on season-long loan
trail: Jack Wilshere passed a medical at Bournemouth on Wednesday evening after agreeing to join on a season-long loan from Arsenal
body: Jack Wilshere’s pursuit of regular first-team football has seen the Arsenal midfielder join Bournemouth on a season-long loan in a move that underlines the club’s remarkable rise from basement division to elite over the past six years. Wilshere, who has been limited to two substitute appearances this season, was omitted from Sam Allardyce’s first England squad on Sunday having effectively fallen behind Granit Xhaka, Mohamed Elneny and Santi Cazorla in central midfield at Arsenal. Arsène Wenger granted him permission to seek a move from the Emirates Stadium to gain more game time after two injury-ravaged seasons. His availability had sparked interest from over 20 clubs from England and across Europe and with various agents mobilised to sound out suitors, Wilshere had earmarked the offers from Bournemouth, Crystal Palace, Roma and Milan for particular attention. He met Eddie Howe and Alan Pardew respectively for talks on Tuesday, and spoke with the former Tottenham Hotspur director of football Franco Baldini, who is now working as a transfer consultant for Roma, on Wednesday. Yet, while the player was open to the idea of moving abroad, neither Roma nor Milan could reach agreement over the financial settlement with Arsenal, who had also made clear they would not countenance his loan to a club they consider a direct rival for a top-four finish. Talks therefore took place with both Bournemouth, who were willing to pay the player’s £90,000-a-week wage and a £2m loan fee, and Palace, with the latter understood to be seeking to pay only a proportion of the salary of a player who last played 90 minutes in a Premier League fixture in September 2014. If that had seen Arsenal favour the switch to the south coast club, Howe also won over Wilshere in lengthy talks after insisting the style of play at the club would suit him, as well as detailing the integral role he could play in the team. The presence of Benik Afobe, a former Arsenal team-mate and godfather to Wilshere’s child, at the Vitality Stadium may also have helped persuade the 24-year-old to move south. Afobe was there to welcome the midfielder as he arrived at the ground to undertake his medical, with his debut a home fixture against West Bromwich Albion after the international window. The player’s impact at Bournemouth, who languished in League Two in 2009‑10, will be key if he is to convince Wenger that he can prolong his career at Arsenal. Wilshere has two years to run on his current contract at the Emirates, with negotiations yet to commence over an extension. He becomes Howe’s eighth signing of the summer – his team have gained a solitary point from their first three games of term – with the midfielder Eunan O’Kane sold to Leeds for an undisclosed fee and Rhoys Wiggins and Baily Cargill loaned to Birmingham and Gillingham respectively. “Jack is a fantastic addition to the club,” said Bournemouth’s chief executive Neill Blake. “He is a player that needs no introduction and one that, quite rightly, our supporters will be excited to see in a Bournemouth shirt. He will bring a wealth of international and Premier League experience, so we are delighted to be able to welcome a player of his calibre to the club.”
